title: Make and Destroy One Object
hints: `Tracked t(v); return &t;` is the tempting wrong answer. `t` lives in `make_tracked`'s stack frame and is destroyed at the closing brace, so the caller reads a dead object (AddressSanitizer calls it `stack-use-after-return`). You need storage that survives the return.

`new Tracked(v)` constructs the object on the heap and hands back a `Tracked*`. It stays alive until someone runs `delete` on that pointer. `delete nullptr` is defined to do nothing, so `destroy_tracked` needs no null check.
